narrative:
The model estimates a 48% chance that you will leave your job, which is high enough for the company to deny your promotion as a precaution.

Three factors shaped this outlook most strongly. First, your overall work experience of 1-5 years pulled the prediction toward staying; most employees the model expects to remain also fall in this early-career range, so the system sees you as typical of loyal, newer staff. However, two other influences pushed harder in the opposite direction. The model noted that you have received other job offers while working here, something that strongly signals higher turnover risk. It also observed that you have spent 1-5 years in your current role, which is common among people the system predicts will leave rather than build longer tenure.

Taken together, the fresh external opportunities and the relatively short time in this position outweighed the stabilizing effect of your limited total experience, tipping the balance toward expecting you to depart.

The company should discuss retention openly with you, explore what would make you want to stay longer, and consider faster promotion paths for high-potential early-career talent. You may want to reflect on whether the external offers better match your goals. Addressing these points now could change the outlook for both sides. (218 words)
